resources.name: Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem
resources.summary: The official access point for the EU Copernicus Sentinel missions: Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical (10 m), Sentinel-3 and Sentinel-5P atmospheric data, with the full mission archives online. Replaces the old Copernicus Open Access Hub (SciHub), which was retired in 2023.
resources.access: Free account at dataspace.copernicus.eu; browse in Copernicus Browser, or script against the STAC and OData APIs at catalogue.dataspace.copernicus.eu; S3-compatible access is also offered.
resources.notes: Per-account service quotas (concurrent connections, monthly transfer) apply to the free tier but are ample for individual research. Processing on the platform uses the separate openEO credit system (see the openEO entry).

resources.name: Copernicus Climate Data Store (ERA5)
resources.summary: Home of ERA5, the ECMWF global reanalysis: hourly fields from 1940 to near-present at 0.25 deg (ERA5-Land at 0.1 deg from 1950), plus seasonal forecasts, satellite climate records and sectoral climate indicators.
resources.access: Register free at cds.climate.copernicus.eu, put the API key in ~/.cdsapirc, then `pip install cdsapi` and submit retrieval requests in Python; a web download form exists for small requests.
resources.notes: Requests are queued; large ERA5 pulls can wait hours. Learn to request only the variables/levels/area you need. For quick point extractions of ERA5, the Open-Meteo historical API is much faster.

resources.name: Copernicus Marine Service
resources.summary: Free EU service distributing global and regional ocean analyses, forecasts, reanalyses and satellite ocean products (temperature, salinity, currents, sea level, biogeochemistry, sea ice).
resources.access: Free registration at data.marine.copernicus.eu, then `pip install copernicusmarine`; the CLI/Python toolbox (`copernicusmarine subset`) downloads regional and temporal cuts without fetching whole files.
resources.notes: Product catalogue is large and naming is bureaucratic; use the web catalogue to find the product ID before scripting.

resources.name: NASA Earthdata
resources.summary: Single free login for NASA's petabyte-scale Earth observation holdings across 12 thematic DAACs: MODIS, VIIRS, ICESat-2, GRACE, GPM precipitation, SMAP soil moisture, NISAR and much more.
resources.access: Create a free Earthdata Login at urs.earthdata.nasa.gov; then `pip install earthaccess` and use earthaccess.search_data()/.download() (handles authentication), or search interactively at search.earthdata.nasa.gov.
resources.notes: Data are increasingly served from AWS (Earthdata Cloud); direct in-region S3 access is free only from us-west-2, but HTTPS download works from anywhere.

resources.name: USGS EarthExplorer
resources.summary: Download portal for the full Landsat archive (1972-present, 30 m multispectral since 1982) plus declassified spy imagery, aerial photos and other USGS collections. All Landsat data have been free since 2008.
resources.access: Web interface at earthexplorer.usgs.gov (free account required to download); bulk/scripted ordering via the Machine-to-Machine (M2M) API after requesting access approval from your profile.
resources.notes: M2M API access requires a separate (free) approval step. Landsat Collection 2 is also mirrored on AWS and Google Cloud as COGs, which is often easier for scripted work.

resources.name: NOAA NCEI / Climate Data Online (GHCN)
resources.summary: World's largest archive of land-station climate records: GHCN-daily covers 100,000+ stations in 180 countries, with monthly (GHCNm) and hourly (GHCNh, replacing ISD) companions.
resources.access: Web search/cart at ncei.noaa.gov/cdo-web; REST API v2 with a free token (limits: 5 requests/s, 10,000 requests/day); raw GHCN flat files are direct download and also mirrored on AWS Open Data (s3://noaa-ghcn-pds).
resources.notes: Token needed only for the CDO API, not for bulk file download. Some derived NOAA products were retired in 2025 amid budget cuts (e.g. the Billion-Dollar Disasters product); the core station archives remain, but check product pages for status.

resources.name: NASA POWER
resources.summary: Analysis-ready daily/hourly/monthly solar radiation and meteorology (from MERRA-2 and CERES) for any point on the globe, from the 1980s to near-present. Designed for agronomy, renewable energy and building science.
resources.access: REST API at power.larc.nasa.gov/api with no key: point, regional and climatology endpoints returning JSON/CSV; also a web Data Access Viewer for interactive download.
resources.notes: Gridded at coarse reanalysis resolution (~0.5 deg); fine for time series at a site, not for spatial detail.

resources.name: Open-Meteo
resources.summary: Open-source weather API serving forecasts from multiple national models plus a gap-free historical archive built on ERA5 (0.25 deg, from 1940) and ERA5-Land (0.1 deg, from 1950). Data are redistributed under CC-BY 4.0.
resources.access: Plain HTTPS, no key, e.g. https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=..&longitude=..&start_date=..&daily=temperature_2m_max; `pip install openmeteo-requests` for a typed client.
resources.notes: Free for non-commercial use up to roughly 10,000 calls/day; commercial or heavier use requires a paid plan. Far quicker than the Copernicus CDS for point-based ERA5 extraction.

resources.name: CMIP6 via ESGF
resources.summary: The Earth System Grid Federation distributes the complete CMIP6 archive (and growing CMIP7 holdings): output from dozens of modelling centres for historical, scenario (SSP) and idealised experiments.
resources.access: Search with the Metagrid interface at esgf-node.llnl.gov (mirrors at DKRZ, CEDA, IPSL), download via generated wget scripts or Globus; for laptop-scale work use the analysis-ready Zarr mirrors on Google Cloud/AWS through `pip install intake-esm` and the Pangeo CMIP6 catalog.
resources.notes: Most CMIP6 data are CC-licensed and need no login; a few older restricted datasets require an ESGF account. Volumes are huge - subset by variable/experiment/model before downloading, or work from the cloud Zarr stores.

resources.name: PANGAEA
resources.summary: Long-running open-access publisher and archive for georeferenced earth and environmental science data (hosted by AWI/MARUM, Germany); every dataset is curated, DOI-minted and citable.
resources.access: Web search at pangaea.de with direct download (mostly tab-delimited text); `pip install pangaeapy` for scripted retrieval by DOI.
resources.notes: Also a realistic place to publish your own data at no cost (curation is free), which satisfies journal data-availability requirements. A minority of datasets are under temporary moratorium.

resources.name: GEBCO
resources.summary: The standard freely available global ocean depth/land elevation grid at 15 arc-second spacing. The GEBCO_2026 grid (published 23 April 2026) incorporates Seabed 2030 contributions; 28.7% of the ocean floor is now mapped to modern standards.
resources.access: Direct download of the global netCDF or user-defined tiles (netCDF/GeoTIFF/ASCII) at download.gebco.net; also served via OPeNDAP.
resources.notes: Away from surveyed tracks, depths are interpolated from satellite altimetry - fine for context maps, not for navigation or fine-scale seafloor work. A type-identifier grid tells you which cells are real measurements.

resources.name: OpenTopography
resources.summary: NSF-funded portal for high-resolution topography: hundreds of airborne/terrestrial lidar point clouds plus on-demand access to global DEMs (SRTM, Copernicus GLO-30/90, NASADEM, ArcticDEM, REMA) with server-side processing.
resources.access: Free account generates an API key instantly; REST endpoint /API/globaldem returns clipped DEMs; web portal for lidar jobs; the QGIS 'OpenTopography DEM Downloader' plugin wraps the API.
resources.notes: Global-DEM API is rate-limited: 200 calls/day with an academic (.edu-verified) key, 50/day otherwise; ~4x4 degree area cap per request. Higher limits need a paid OpenTopography Plus subscription. Lidar holdings are US-heavy.

resources.name: EarthScope (SAGE/IRIS) Data Services
resources.summary: The NSF national archive for seismological data (formerly the IRIS DMC): decades of continuous waveforms and station metadata from thousands of seismometers worldwide, served through standard FDSN web services.
resources.access: FDSN web services now at service.earthscope.org (migrated from service.iris.edu); in Python `pip install obspy` then Client('IRIS').get_waveforms(net, sta, loc, chan, t1, t2) - ObsPy follows the redirects.
resources.notes: Mid-migration to the cloud in 2026: fdsnws-dataselect and fdsnws-station have moved hosts, and the irisws-timeseries processing service is retired as of 26 Aug 2026 (do processing client-side with ObsPy instead). A small subset of networks embargo recent data.

resources.name: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program (ComCat)
resources.summary: Authoritative global earthquake catalogue (ANSS ComCat) with locations, magnitudes, moment tensors, ShakeMap and PAGER products, plus real-time GeoJSON feeds updated every minute.
resources.access: Real-time GeoJSON feeds at earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed; historical queries via the fdsnws-event API (also reachable from ObsPy's FDSN client); interactive search on the website.
resources.notes: Query results capped (20,000 events per request) - page by time window for bulk pulls. Global completeness is roughly M4.5+; use regional catalogues for smaller events outside the US.

resources.name: Argo
resources.summary: Global array of ~4,000 autonomous floats profiling temperature and salinity in the upper 2,000 m (Deep Argo to 6,000 m; BGC-Argo adds oxygen, pH, nitrate and more). Over 3 million profiles collected since 2000 (3-millionth in July 2024), about 100,000 per year, all free.
resources.access: `pip install argopy` for a pandas/xarray interface with regional/float/profile fetchers; raw netCDF from the Ifremer and US GODAE GDACs via HTTPS/S3; several ERDDAP servers also serve Argo.
resources.notes: Use delayed-mode (quality-controlled) data for science where available; real-time data carry only automated QC. File structure is fiddly - argopy exists precisely to hide it.

resources.name: EM-DAT
resources.summary: The international disaster database maintained by CRED (UCLouvain): standardised records of natural and technological disasters worldwide since 1900, with deaths, people affected and economic losses per event.
resources.access: Register free at public.emdat.be (non-commercial use), then download the full database as .xlsx from the Access Data tab.
resources.notes: Commercial use requires a paid subscription. Entry threshold (10+ deaths, 100+ affected, emergency declaration or international appeal) and reporting practices changed over time - be careful with long trend analyses; pre-2000 records are flagged as lower quality.

resources.name: OpenStreetMap (Geofabrik & Overpass)
resources.summary: Crowd-sourced global geodatabase of roads, buildings, land use, waterways and POIs - the de facto free base vector layer for environmental and hazards research.
resources.access: Country/region extracts updated daily at download.geofabrik.de (no registration); ad-hoc spatial queries via the Overpass API (try overpass-turbo.eu); `pip install osmnx` for street networks and features in Python.
resources.notes: ODbL licence: derived databases must be shared under compatible terms - fine for research, but read it before mixing with proprietary data. Public Overpass instances enforce fair-use limits; heavy jobs should use Geofabrik extracts locally.

resources.name: OpenAerialMap
resources.summary: Open catalogue of openly licensed (CC-BY 4.0) aerial and drone imagery, heavily used after disasters via the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap community; imagery is served as cloud-optimised GeoTIFFs and web tiles.
resources.access: Browse and download at map.openaerialmap.org; programmatic search via the API at api.openaerialmap.org; anyone can also upload imagery.
resources.notes: Coverage is patchy by design - dense where mapping campaigns or disasters occurred, absent elsewhere. Check acquisition dates carefully.

resources.name: Global Forest Watch
resources.summary: WRI platform serving the Hansen/UMD global tree-cover-loss dataset (30 m, annual from 2001, updated yearly) plus near-real-time deforestation and fire alerts (GLAD, RADD) and carbon layers.
resources.access: Interactive dashboards at globalforestwatch.org (no login); bulk data via the Open Data Portal (data.globalforestwatch.org) and the Data API (data-api.globalforestwatch.org); analysis in a country/AOI is point-and-click.
resources.notes: 'Tree cover loss' is not the same as deforestation (includes harvest, fire, plantations); the makers themselves warn against naive year-over-year trend comparisons across sensor-era changes.

resources.name: WorldClim
resources.summary: Standard global climate surfaces for ecology and species distribution modelling: monthly temperature/precipitation climatologies for 1970-2000 at four resolutions down to 30 arc-seconds (~1 km), the 19 'bioclim' variables, and CMIP6-based downscaled future projections.
resources.access: Direct download of GeoTIFF zips at worldclim.org (no registration); read with terra (R) or rioxarray (Python).
resources.notes: Baseline period is 1970-2000 - already far from current climate; interpolation quality degrades where stations are sparse (tropics, mountains). Compare with CHELSA before committing.

resources.name: CHELSA
resources.summary: Downscaled global climate dataset at 30 arc-seconds (~1 km) built from ERA-Interim/ERA5 with orographic corrections; monthly climatologies (1981-2010), bioclim variables, time series and CMIP downscaled scenarios. Often outperforms station-interpolated products in mountains and data-sparse regions.
resources.access: Direct download of GeoTIFFs from the site's download section (S3-hosted; wget file lists provided); no registration.
resources.notes: Files are large (global 1 km layers); download per-variable and clip early. Cite the specific version (V2.1 is current).

resources.name: SoilGrids
resources.summary: ISRIC's machine-learning global soil maps at 250 m: pH, organic carbon, texture fractions, bulk density, nitrogen and more at six standard depths, each with uncertainty layers.
resources.access: Web viewer at soilgrids.org; point queries via the REST API at rest.isric.org; full maps as cloud-optimised GeoTIFFs/VRTs at files.isric.org or via WCS at maps.isric.org.
resources.notes: Global model predictions, not survey maps - uncertainty is substantial in under-sampled regions; always propagate the provided uncertainty layers rather than treating values as ground truth.

resources.name: GBIF
resources.summary: Global Biodiversity Information Facility: 3.1+ billion species occurrence records from over 2,500 publishing institutions, integrated with a common taxonomy and standard (Darwin Core).
resources.access: Search API at api.gbif.org/v1 needs no key; citable bulk downloads (with DOI) require a free gbif.org account; `pip install pygbif` or R package rgbif; full snapshots on AWS/Azure open data.
resources.notes: Occurrence data carry strong spatial and taxonomic sampling biases and variable coordinate precision - filter by issues/flags before analysis. Cite the download DOI, not 'GBIF' generically.

resources.name: NASA FIRMS
resources.summary: Fire Information for Resource Management System: near-real-time active-fire detections from VIIRS (375 m) and MODIS (1 km), typically available within ~3 hours of overpass, plus the full detection archive back to 2000 (MODIS).
resources.access: Interactive fire map needs no login; for data, request a free MAP_KEY (instant, email) and pull CSV/JSON via the area API, or order archive downloads.
resources.notes: Detections are thermal anomalies, not confirmed fires (gas flares, volcanoes and sun glint appear); cloud cover causes misses. API keys have transaction limits per 10-minute window.

resources.name: Natural Earth
resources.summary: Public-domain vector and raster basemap data at 1:10m, 1:50m and 1:110m scales - coastlines, countries, rivers, lakes, populated places - built for making clean small-scale maps.
resources.access: Direct download (shapefiles/GeoPackage/rasters) at naturalearthdata.com; also fetchable from cartopy and geopandas helper functions.
resources.notes: Public domain, so no attribution legally required (though appreciated). Boundaries follow de facto control; check the disputed-areas layers if that matters for your maps.

resources.name: Google Earth Engine
resources.summary: Cloud platform co-locating a multi-petabyte catalog (Landsat, Sentinel, MODIS, climate and land-cover products) with parallel compute, so continental-scale analyses run without downloading anything.
resources.access: Register a Google Cloud project for noncommercial use (eligibility questionnaire in the Cloud Console), then use the JavaScript Code Editor at code.earthengine.google.com or `pip install earthengine-api` (plus geemap for interactive maps).
resources.notes: Since 27 April 2026 noncommercial projects have monthly compute quotas: Community tier 150 EECU-hours; Contributor tier 1,000 EECU-hours (free but requires attaching a billing account); Partner tier (100,000 EECU-hours) by application for sustainability-focused organisations. Exceeding quota throttles rather than blocks. Commercial use is paid.

resources.name: Microsoft Planetary Computer
resources.subcategory: open EO data catalog + STAC API
resources.summary: Open STAC catalog and API over petabytes of analysis-ready geospatial data on Azure (Sentinel-1/2, Landsat, NAIP, Copernicus DEM, ERA5, land cover and more), with free anonymous read access to most collections.
resources.access: STAC API at planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1; `pip install planetary-computer pystac-client`, search, then sign asset URLs with planetary_computer.sign(); browse collections on the website.
resources.notes: The free hosted JupyterHub was retired in June 2024 - you bring your own compute (a laptop or Colab works; data egress is free over HTTPS). 'Planetary Computer Pro' (GA June 2026) is a separate paid Azure enterprise product; the open catalog remains free.

resources.name: openEO on Copernicus Data Space
resources.summary: Standardised processing API for Sentinel data in the cloud: build workflows (e.g. cloud-free composites, NDVI time series) that execute next to the data. Every free CDSE account gets 10,000 openEO credits per month.
resources.access: `pip install openeo`, connect to openeo.dataspace.copernicus.eu, authenticate with the free CDSE account, build a process graph and run it as a batch job; a web editor exists for no-code use.
resources.notes: Credits reset monthly and do not roll over; a March 2026 billing update cut typical credit consumption ~25%, but large jobs still exhaust the free allocation - test on small extents first. Bigger quotas via paid CREODIAS credits or ESA Network of Resources sponsorship.

resources.name: QGIS
resources.summary: The leading open-source desktop GIS: visualisation, editing, analysis and cartography for raster and vector data, with a large plugin ecosystem and Python (PyQGIS) scripting.
resources.access: Installers for Windows/macOS/Linux at qgis.org; install plugins (e.g. OpenTopography downloader, QuickMapServices) from the built-in manager.
resources.notes: Use the Long Term Release (LTR) for stability. Runs fine on modest laptops for most tasks.

resources.name: GDAL/OGR
resources.summary: The translator library underneath nearly all open geospatial software, reading and writing hundreds of raster and vector formats; its CLI tools do reprojection, mosaicking, clipping and format conversion at scale.
resources.access: `conda install -c conda-forge gdal` (or OS packages); command-line tools gdal_translate, gdalwarp, ogr2ogr, gdalbuildvrt plus Python bindings.
resources.notes: Prefer conda-forge or OS packages over pip for a working build with all drivers. Learning the CLI pays off more than the raw Python bindings (or use rasterio/rioxarray on top).

resources.name: GeoPandas
resources.summary: Pandas extended with geometry columns: file I/O for all OGR formats, spatial joins, overlays, projections and quick plotting - the standard Python entry point for vector geodata.
resources.access: `pip install geopandas`; gpd.read_file() for any vector format, .explore() renders an interactive web map in one line.
resources.notes: Memory-bound for very large layers; pair with pyogrio (default engine in recent versions) and spatial filters at read time.

resources.name: xarray (+ rioxarray)
resources.summary: The core Python library for gridded earth data: labelled multi-dimensional arrays with named coordinates, reading netCDF, Zarr and GRIB (via cfgrib), and scaling past RAM with Dask. rioxarray adds CRS-aware raster I/O on top.
resources.access: `pip install xarray rioxarray dask`; xr.open_dataset('era5.nc') then .sel(time=..., latitude=...) for label-based subsetting.
resources.notes: The whole modern climate/EO Python stack (Pangeo) is built around it - worth learning properly via Project Pythia before touching big datasets.

resources.name: Climate Data Operators (CDO)
resources.summary: Max Planck Institute's command-line toolkit with hundreds of chainable operators for netCDF/GRIB climate files: regridding, temporal statistics, ensemble math, field selection - the workhorse of CMIP-style processing.
resources.access: `conda install -c conda-forge cdo`; operators chain right-to-left, e.g. `cdo -yearmean -selname,tas input.nc out.nc`.
resources.notes: Terse syntax and cryptic errors, but far faster than naive Python loops for bulk file processing; NCO is the complementary tool for attribute/metadata surgery.

resources.name: GRASS GIS
resources.summary: Veteran open-source GIS (development since 1982) with 400+ analysis modules, particularly strong in hydrology, terrain analysis and large-raster processing; scriptable from Python and callable from QGIS.
resources.access: Download at grass.osgeo.org (or OSGeo4W/conda); use standalone, through the QGIS processing toolbox, or via grass.script / grass.jupyter in Python.
resources.notes: The location/mapset data model confuses newcomers; if you only need one watershed delineation, the QGIS-GRASS integration is the gentler route.

resources.name: ObsPy
resources.summary: The standard Python framework for seismology: reads all common waveform formats (miniSEED, SAC), speaks FDSN web services for data download, and provides filtering, instrument-response removal, triggering and plotting.
resources.access: `pip install obspy`; read('file.mseed') for local data, Client('IRIS').get_waveforms(...) for remote archives.
resources.notes: Its tutorial gallery doubles as a seismic data processing course. Update to a recent version so FDSN endpoints (EarthScope migration) resolve correctly.

resources.name: PyGMT
resources.summary: Python interface to the Generic Mapping Tools (GMT 6), the geoscience community's standard for publication-quality maps, gridding and geodesy-aware plotting; ships with easy access to remote datasets like Earth relief.
resources.access: `conda install -c conda-forge pygmt`; fig = pygmt.Figure(); fig.coast(...); fig.grdimage('@earth_relief_01m', region=[...]).
resources.notes: Conda installation strongly recommended (needs the GMT C library). Classic GMT shell syntax remains available if you inherit old scripts.

resources.name: Leafmap
resources.summary: Python package for interactive geospatial visualisation and analysis in Jupyter with minimal code: drag-and-drop layers, basemap gallery, COG/STAC support, and split-map comparisons; sibling of geemap (same author) for Earth Engine.
resources.access: `pip install leafmap`; m = leafmap.Map(); m.add_raster('dem.tif'); works with ipyleaflet, folium and MapLibre backends.
resources.notes: Visualisation-first: for heavy processing you still drop down to GDAL/xarray, but for exploring data it is the fastest on-ramp in the Python ecosystem.

resources.name: EarthArXiv
resources.summary: Community-run preprint server for all of earth and planetary science, operating since 2017; volunteer-moderated for scope (not scientific quality), with each preprint receiving a DOI, typically online within days.
resources.access: Submit or read free at eartharxiv.org; simple account for submission, none for reading.
resources.notes: Check your target journal's preprint policy before posting (most earth-science journals allow it). Postprints (accepted versions) are also accepted where journal policy permits.

resources.name: EGUsphere
resources.summary: Copernicus/EGU's preprint repository and discussion platform: standalone preprints plus every manuscript in EGU journals' interactive public peer review, where referee reports, community comments and author replies are all published.
resources.access: Read everything without an account at egusphere.copernicus.org; post preprints or community comments with a free Copernicus account.
resources.notes: Reading the open review threads of published papers is an underused (free) education in how peer review actually works in the field.

resources.name: NASA Science Explorer (SciX)
resources.summary: Free literature discovery system extending the NASA ADS to earth science, planetary science, heliophysics and astrophysics: 20+ million records including all AGU and EGU journals, arXiv/EarthArXiv preprints, abstracts and grey literature, with citation links to data and software.
resources.access: Search free at scixplorer.org; optional account for saved libraries and email alerts; scripted access via the ADS/SciX API with a free api-key.
resources.notes: Indexes metadata and links out to full text - paywalled papers stay paywalled, but the preprint/open-access links it surfaces are often enough. Citation coverage in earth science is still filling in compared with astronomy.

resources.name: Copernicus Publications (EGU journals)
resources.summary: Publisher of the 19 EGU open-access journals (ACP, TC - The Cryosphere, GMD, HESS, SE and others), all with public interactive peer review via EGUsphere; everything is free to read under CC-BY.
resources.access: Submit through each journal's site (e.g. atmospheric-chemistry-and-physics.net); manuscripts appear as public preprints during review.
resources.notes: Publishing costs an APC (single per-article charge since Jan 2025), but waivers are automatic for corresponding authors in Research4Life group A & B countries, 50% off in European economically disadvantaged countries, 10% off for EGU members, and case-by-case waivers exist for anyone who cannot pay - a realistic route for unfunded authors.

resources.name: Seismica
resources.summary: Community-led diamond open-access journal for seismology and earthquake science, open for submissions since 2022: no fees to publish or read, run by a volunteer board of ~47 researchers, hosted by McGill University Library.
resources.access: Submit via the OJS system at seismica.library.mcgill.ca; LaTeX/Word templates provided.
resources.notes: Peer review is thorough; volunteer editorial capacity means timelines can be slower than commercial journals. Publishes reports, fast reports and null-results articles.

resources.name: Volcanica
resources.summary: The first diamond open-access journal in the geosciences (since 2018): peer-reviewed volcanology research free for both authors and readers, and the model that Seismica, Tektonika and Sedimentologika later followed.
resources.access: Submit at jvolcanica.org (OJS); all articles CC-BY.
resources.notes: Sister diamond-OA journals now cover tectonics (Tektonika) and sedimentology (Sedimentologika) if your subfield fits those instead.

resources.name: National Geographic Society Grants
resources.summary: Funds individual 'Explorers' worldwide for field-based science, conservation, storytelling and education; historically Level I grants up to USD 20,000 and Level II up to USD 100,000, and no institutional affiliation is required.
resources.access: Apply online to an open Request for Proposals on the NGS funding-opportunities page; budgets and eligibility are defined per RFP.
resources.notes: The program has shifted from standing open calls to time-bound, themed RFPs - check what is currently open rather than assuming the old Level I/II cycle. Highly competitive; strong fit with the RFP theme matters more than CV.

resources.name: Rufford Small Grants
resources.summary: UK foundation funding early-career conservationists for fieldwork in developing countries: staged grants of up to GBP 7,000 (1st), 8,000 (2nd), 12,000 (Booster) and 18,000 (Completion); rolling applications with no deadlines.
resources.access: Apply any time at apply.ruffordsmallgrants.org; one application per 12 months.
resources.notes: Project must be in an eligible (developing) country and have a genuine conservation focus - pure research without conservation outcomes, expeditions and conference travel are explicitly not funded. Priority to current/recent MSc-PhD researchers.

resources.name: EGU travel support (Roland Schlich)
resources.summary: EGU's travel support scheme for its General Assembly, aimed at early-career scientists and researchers from low- and middle-income countries: registration-fee waiver plus a travel stipend for selected applicants.
resources.access: Apply during the abstract-submission window (typically closing early December for the spring assembly) by ticking the support application with your abstract.
resources.notes: Covers only part of total costs and is competitive; the fully virtual participation option in recent assemblies is the cheaper fallback. AGU runs comparable student travel grants for its Fall Meeting.

resources.name: ESA Network of Resources (NoR) Sponsorship
resources.summary: ESA scheme that pays for cloud EO processing resources (on platforms such as CREODIAS/Copernicus Data Space services, commercial EO platforms and datasets) for research, education and pre-commercial projects - typically for periods up to about a year.
resources.access: Pick services in the NoR portal 'wizard' at nor-discover.org, then submit the sponsorship request form with a short project description; approved projects get the resources at no cost.
resources.notes: Sponsorship covers platform resources, not salaries. Aimed at European/ESA-member-state users primarily - check eligibility per service; modest requests from students and researchers are routinely approved.

resources.name: Project Pythia
resources.summary: The Pangeo-affiliated education hub for geoscientific Python: 'Pythia Foundations' teaches the core stack (Python, Jupyter, NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, xarray, Cartopy) and a growing set of domain 'Cookbooks' show full workflows on real datasets.
resources.access: All material free online at projectpythia.org as executable Jupyter Books; run in the browser via Binder or locally.
resources.notes: This is the on-ramp the community itself points newcomers to; NSF/Unidata-backed and actively maintained.

resources.name: NASA ARSET
resources.summary: NASA's Applied Remote Sensing Training program: free live webinars and a large on-demand archive teaching practical use of satellite data for air quality, water, disasters, land and climate applications, offered at introductory through advanced levels, many in English and Spanish.
resources.access: Register free for live sessions or watch recorded trainings and slides on the ARSET site; certificates of completion for live series.
resources.notes: Trainings use free tools and data (Giovanni, Worldview, Earth Engine, QGIS), so everything is reproducible without institutional resources.

resources.name: Data Carpentry Geospatial Workshop
resources.summary: The Carpentries' peer-reviewed, CC-BY lesson series introducing raster and vector geospatial data and analysis in R (with community-developed Python equivalents), built for researchers with no GIS background.
resources.access: All lessons free online for self-study; live workshops run worldwide by volunteer instructors (find one via carpentries.org).
resources.notes: Self-study works fine; the datasets and setup instructions are included. Some hosted workshops charge a small venue fee, the materials never do.

resources.name: EO College
resources.summary: Free online learning hub for earth observation (University of Jena / ESA-affiliated), best known for radar remote sensing: the 'Echoes in Space' SAR MOOC, SAR-EDU materials, and courses on optical EO and applications, with completion certificates.
resources.access: Free account at eo-college.org, then enrol in self-paced courses.
resources.notes: The SAR material fills a genuine gap - few free structured courses on radar exist elsewhere. Course production pace varies with project funding cycles.

resources.name: An Introduction to Earth and Environmental Data Science
resources.summary: Free Jupyter Book from Ryan Abernathey's Columbia course 'Research Computing in Earth Science': the JupyterLab/Git/Python/xarray/Dask workflow used in modern computational geoscience, with assignments on real data.
resources.access: Read free online; all notebooks runnable locally or on free cloud notebooks.
resources.notes: Assumes basic programming willingness; pairs naturally with Project Pythia (same ecosystem, same authors' community).

resources.name: Pangeo
resources.summary: Open community building and supporting the scalable Python geoscience stack (xarray, Dask, Zarr, Jupyter); its Discourse forum is where the practitioners who wrote those tools answer data-handling questions, and it runs regular open community meetings and showcases.
resources.access: Forum at discourse.pangeo.io (free account); community calls and resources listed at pangeo.io.
resources.notes: Best forum on the internet for 'how do I process this 2 TB of CMIP6/Sentinel data on limited hardware' questions; searching past threads often solves the problem outright.

resources.name: Software Underground
resources.summary: Grass-roots community of 4,500+ 'digital subsurface' professionals - geologists, geophysicists, engineers - with an active chat (self-hosted Mattermost, moved off Slack), hackathons and the curated awesome-open-geoscience list.
resources.access: Join free at softwareunderground.org; chat at mattermost.softwareunderground.org.
resources.notes: Leans toward subsurface/energy geoscience; industry practitioners are unusually generous with practical code help here.

resources.name: GIS Stack Exchange
resources.summary: The main Q&A site for geographic information systems: hundreds of thousands of answered questions on QGIS, GDAL, PostGIS, coordinate systems and Python geospatial tooling, searchable without an account.
resources.access: Read and search free, no account; free registration to ask or answer.
resources.notes: For domain science questions (geology, meteorology, oceanography) rather than tooling, the smaller Earth Science Stack Exchange (earthscience.stackexchange.com) is the counterpart.
